text:
sam: FYI ran a smoke canary after the kernel-selection change. short-request p95 spiked ~20ms. looks host-side.

sam: quick flame and syscall dump points at an extra normalization pass + many tiny grpc writes during parse/tokenize.

nina: do you have the trace snippets?

sam: pasted abbreviated profile below (host parse area):
```
copy_normalize_bytes  28.1%  28.1%  2.2s
grpc_write_small  21.4%  49.5%  1.65s
tokenizer_main  13.8%  63.3%  1.06s
kv_lookup  8.5%  71.8%  0.65s
batching_timer  3.2%  75.0%  0.24s
```

sam: additionally kv shard scatter increased; more keys landing on many shards -> higher eviction churn.

oscar: what exactly changed in the chooser?

sam: chooser prefers our new fused-attention kernel for len < 64. fused kernel requires inputs to be in the trimmed-normalized layout. to be conservative we run a host-side normalize step always if chooser picks fused. that step does a small memcopy and creates shorter framed writes downstream.

nina: ah, so added host work + network write overhead. two levers: avoid the normalize when safe, or coalesce writes in the proxy.

oscar: proxy writev/coalesce is low-risk. can we toggle it for the canary?

aria: quick experiment: enabled writev coalescing + increased grpc small write batch to 6. config snippet we used:
```
proxy.coalesce.enabled = true
proxy.coalesce.max_bytes = 8192
proxy.coalesce.max_writes = 6
```

aria: after 20m of steady traffic: syscalls down ~35%, p95 down ~14ms, kv-evictions down ~12%.

oscar: good win. but we still see shard spread on hot keys?

sam: yes. hypothesis: the host metadata included request-id + route + some ephemeral flags in the key -> keys not canonical across identical user prompts. small writes causing different framing -> different key hashes on proxy-side sharding.

nina: we should canonicalize the KV key at host before lookup: drop ephemeral bits, stable serialize. also add a key fingerprint telemetry to measure fanout.

oscar: for batching: would a session-affinity micro-window help? e.g., if the same session sends another short request within 12ms, keep it in the same batch window. decreases first-token latency slightly for repeated interactive flows but improves batching for tails.

sam: ran a microbenchmark for sticky-window=12ms (only for active sessions): batch hit-rate +24% for short requests, p95 improved ~6ms overall in our local harness.

aria: any impact on throughput? tradeoffs?

sam: negligible throughput loss on our test cluster. long sequences unaffected.

nina: on the kernel chooser side: we can publish a per-model capability flag "accepts-raw-layout" to the model catalog. when present, host skip normalize. default remains conservative off. that'll avoid copies for many known open models.

oscar: timeline & owners?

nina: I'll own host KV canonicalization + fingerprint telemetry. will add tests to ensure stable keys across framing variants.

oscar: I'll do a proxy writev toggle PR (unit + perf run) and a quick rollout plan.

sam: I'll add the chooser model flag and a tiny integration test to verify correctness with fused kernel inputs. also adding the sticky-batch experiment to the batching repo.

ci-bot: canary proxy-coalesce v1 deployed -> 2026-03-22T19:05:00Z

aria: short-term plan: keep coalesce on in canary for 2 hours, collect shard-fanout + p95. medium-term: land KV canonicalization and chooser flags.

nina: for metrics, please capture: per-key shard_count, kvcache_evictions, host_parse_syscalls, small_write_rate, batch_hit_rate.

oscar: i'll also add a debug dump that can be enabled per-request to capture raw frames for a sample of traffic (privacy-safe).

sam: action items recap: (1) proxy writev toggle + perf runs (oscar) (2) KV key canonicalization + telemetry (nina) (3) chooser per-model raw-layout flag + tests (sam) (4) sticky-batching experiment instrumentation (sam/aria).

aria: thanks team. let's avoid landing the chooser change globally until we have canonical keys telemetry.

nina: agreed. will open draft PR today.

oscar: PR for proxy coalesce incoming in ~1h with perf numbers.
